data.name: Finn
data.gender_notes: Finn is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Irish word 'finne' meaning fair or white. In Irish mythology, Finn was the name of a legendary warrior, and in the Finnish language, it means 'thunder'. In the Christian context, Finn may symbolize purity and innocence. The name Finn carries the meaning “Fair or White” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Finn usually hope their child will grow to embody fair or white and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Finn belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fair or White.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Finn total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_greek.name: Φίνν
in_greek.meaning: Φίνν σημαίνει το φιλικό ή τον λευκό
in_greek.long_meaning: Φίνν είναι η ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος Φινν, που προέρχεται από την ιρλανδική γλώσσα και σημαίνει το φιλικό ή τον λευκό. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, το όνομα Φίνν συνδέεται με την έννοια της φιλίας και της αγνότητας.

in_latin.name: Finn
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Finnus originem habet in lingua hibernica et significat albus vel fair. In traditione christiana, nomen Finnus saepe coniungitur cum virtutibus puritatis et candoris.

in_english.name: Finn
in_english.meaning: Finn means fair, white, or clear

In Christian tradition, Finn is often linked to virtues of purity and clarity. The name has been popularized in various cultures, including Irish and English-speaking countries.
